source: Alta Badia trail map 2024-25 (skimap.org map 37722, the resort's own PDF): run numbers in coloured circles (blue, red, black), read from the lift table's 'Slope' column and the badges on the map; colours classified by script from the PDF text positions and checked by eye
numbers_note: Numbers that carry two colours on the map are matched by name only, or left to OpenStreetMap: 5 (red from Arlara and Braia Fraida, blue elsewhere), 31 (red from Cherz, blue from Pralongià I), 40 (red from Frara, blue from Plans), 45 (black from Col Pradat, blue from Colfosco). 17 is red for Altin and black for Gran Risa (by name). 1 is red for Boè and black for Vallon (by name; a number never makes a run easier than OpenStreetMap). 2 is blue for Crep de Mont and red where it leaves Boè (OpenStreetMap's Boè - Crep de Mont, already red, stays red).
runs_note: Gran Risa, Vallon and Col Pradat are the black badges on the map; Gardenaccia nera is named 'black' and OpenStreetMap rates it advanced (the map's 25 badge is blue for Gardenaccia B).
lifts_source: lift table on the trail map (chairs and gondolas only; numbers removed, names as OpenStreetMap writes them where only the accent differs)
lifts_note: Surface lifts on the map's table (Codes, Armentarola, Capanna Nera, Pralongià I, Crep de Mont, Abrusé, La Para, Incisa, Pezzei, Col d'Altin, Baby La Crusc, Ferata Gran Risa) are left out of this list. The Lagazuoi cable car (1-01, runs 1 red and 2 black down to Armentarola) starts at Passo Falzarego, outside this map, reached by ski bus or taxi from Armentarola.

elsewhere.Lagazuoi: the Lagazuoi cable car at Passo Falzarego and its runs (Lagazuoi 1 red, 2 black, ending at Armentarola): a separate lift area reached by bus or taxi
